highlights.title: Overview
highlights.value:
Founded in 1887 as the Working Men’s College, RMIT University has evolved into a global leader in technology, design, and enterprise. It is one of Australia's original educational institutions and remains the only university in the country allowed to use the "Royal" prefix and the monarch's coat of arms.

As a dual-sector university, RMIT offers both vocational and higher education, providing flexible pathways across disciplines like Art & Design, Architecture, Engineering, Business, and Computer Science. The university is particularly renowned for its research impact and strong industry integration, ensuring you learn in a real-world context.

highlights.title: Student life
highlights.value:
Life at RMIT is inclusive, with a diverse community representing over 190 nationalities. You can join more than 100 student clubs and societies, ranging from cultural groups to creative communities.

The university places a high priority on your well-being, offering comprehensive support services, including Student Connect (for academic advice and administrative support), Makerspace (creative hubs for innovation), Ngarara Willim Centre (dedicated support for indigenous students) and multi-faith chaplaincy and wellbeing support (to stay healthy and connected).

highlights.title: Accommodation
highlights.value:
RMIT offers various housing options to suit your lifestyle and budget. You can choose from Halls of Residence, shared houses and apartments, and homestays. The university’s accommodation support team can also assist you in finding private rentals or navigating legal agreements.

If you’re looking for budget-friendly accommodation options outside the campus, feel free to download our app and check out the Stays feature!

highlights.title: Facilities
highlights.value:
1. Library

The RMIT University Library system includes major sites like the Swanston Library (City campus), Bundoora Library, and Brunswick Library. You’ll have access to extensive digital collections, dedicated Neurodiverse Study Sessions, and the Adobe Hub, where coaches help you master creative software.

2. Sports

You can stay active through the RMIT Active programme. Facilities include fully-equipped gyms, indoor multi-purpose sports complexes, and outdoor playing fields at the Bundoora and Saigon South campuses. There are also competitive inter-university sports teams you can join.

3. Laboratories

RMIT is home to world-class specialised labs, including those for high-tech engineering research, simulated real-world banking environments, a cyber security and logistics lab and even a flight simulator for aviation students.

4. Cafeteria

Each campus offers a variety of dining spots. At the Melbourne City campus, you’ll be surrounded by the CBD's famous cafes and restaurants. On-campus, you’ll find diverse food outlets providing everything from fresh coffee to international cuisine, ensuring you have plenty of healthy and affordable options between classes.
